summary.text: Jahana Hayes is the Democratic incumbent for Connecticut's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. A Waterbury native, she taught history for 15 years and was named 2016 National Teacher of the Year before running for Congress. She serves on the House Agriculture and Education and Workforce committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Waterbury, Connecticut, in 1973; her official biography describes Waterbury as her hometown.

Earned an associate degree from Naugatuck Valley Community College (2002), a bachelor's degree from Southern Connecticut State University (2005), a master's degree in curriculum and instruction from the University of Saint Joseph (2012), and an advanced degree in educational administration and supervision from the University of Bridgeport (2014).
Taught history for 15 years at John F. Kennedy High School in Waterbury, where she was named Waterbury Teacher of the Year and Connecticut Teacher of the Year.
Named 2016 National Teacher of the Year, and in that role traveled the country and the world as an ambassador for public education.

Elected to the U.S. House in November 2018, defeating Republican Manny Santos, 55.9% to 44.1%; her office describes her as the first African-American woman to represent Connecticut in Congress. She took office in 2019 and is serving her fourth term.

Serves on the House Committee on Education and Workforce and the House Agriculture Committee, where she is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture. In the 117th Congress she chaired the Agriculture subcommittee on Nutrition, Oversight, and Department Operations.
According to her official biography, she has had 11 bills signed into law and has introduced 80 bills.
